summary: AstroGuard AI is an offline-capable astronaut health monitoring and decision-support prototype designed for long-duration space missions. It combines simulated physiological measurements, personalized health baselines, explainable experimental alerts, and astronaut self-assessments to support crew health awareness. The system also simulates delayed communication with Earth, allowing health reports to be queued and synchronized when connectivity returns. NASA Open Science Data Repository studies provide scientific research context, while all simulated measurements and experimental algorithms are clearly identified.
details:
AstroGuard AI - Intelligent Astronaut Health Monitoring Beyond Earth

Problem Statement

Long-duration space missions expose astronauts to physiological and psychological challenges, including cardiovascular changes, disrupted sleep, isolation, and limited access to immediate medical support. Communication delays during deep-space missions can make timely health assessments more difficult.

Proposed Solution

AstroGuard AI is an offline-capable astronaut health-monitoring and decision-support prototype designed to improve crew health awareness and support autonomous health assessment during space missions.

How It Works

AstroGuard AI monitors simulated physiological measurements, including heart rate, blood oxygen saturation, body temperature, and sleep duration. Each astronaut has a personalized baseline against which measurements are compared.

When readings exceed configurable experimental limits, the system generates explainable alerts showing the triggering measurement, baseline deviation, and reason for the flag.

Astronauts can complete self-assessments covering fatigue, stress, sleep quality, symptoms, and recent activity. The system combines these observations with simulated telemetry and recent trends to provide experimental decision-support insights.

A mission timeline records important events, while an offline-capable reporting system queues health reports during simulated Earth communication delays and synchronizes them when connectivity returns.

NASA Research Integration

AstroGuard AI incorporates metadata from five NASA Open Science Data Repository studies: OSD-575, OSD-344, OSD-484, OSD-919, and OSD-969.

These studies provide scientific context about cardiovascular, biological, immune-system, and thermoregulation-related effects associated with spaceflight.

NASA research metadata is clearly separated from synthetic physiological measurements. The prototype does not claim that NASA datasets provide live astronaut telemetry or clinically validated alert thresholds.

Technologies Used

  • Python and Flask for backend development
  • HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for the interface
  • SQLite for local data persistence
  • Interactive data visualization
  • Experimental rule-based anomaly detection
  • NASA Open Science Data Repository metadata
  • Offline synchronization and simulated communication delays

Innovation and Impact

AstroGuard AI combines personalized health monitoring, explainable alerts, self-assessment, and delayed communication handling in one integrated prototype.

Its goal is to demonstrate how astronauts could maintain greater awareness of their well-being and organize health information during missions where immediate communication with Earth may not be available.

Limitations and Future Development

AstroGuard AI is a research prototype using synthetic health measurements and experimental algorithms. It is not a clinically validated medical device.

Future development could include validated physiological datasets, wearable sensor integration, improved predictive analytics, and evaluation with aerospace medical specialists.
